scenes.heading: RDBMS
scenes.subheading: Relational databases built on tables and SQL
scenes.narration: An RDBMS, or relational database management system, organizes data into related tables and lets you query them with SQL.

scenes.heading: Core ideas of an RDBMS
bullets: Data lives in tables of rows and columns
Tables relate to each other through keys
SQL is the language for querying and updating
scenes.narration: In an RDBMS, data lives in tables made of rows and columns, giving it a clear structure. Tables relate to one another through keys, which model real-world relationships. SQL is the standard language you use to query and modify that data. And ACID guarantees ensure transactions are reliable even when many run at once.

scenes.heading: Joining related tables with SQL
scenes.code:
SELECT c.name, o.total
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.total > 100;
scenes.narration: This query shows the relational model in action by joining two tables. The customers and orders tables are linked on customer_id, the key they share. The join stitches related rows together so we can see each customer's order totals. This ability to combine related tables through keys is exactly what makes a system relational.

scenes.heading: RDBMS vs plain tables
scenes.narration: An RDBMS enforces relationships through keys and protects data with ACID transactions. Flat storage has no concept of relationships and offers no transactional guarantees. The relational model's structure and reliability are why RDBMSs remain the backbone of business applications.

scenes.text: An RDBMS combines related tables, SQL, and ACID guarantees into a reliable, structured data store.
scenes.narration: The core message is that an RDBMS unites related tables, SQL, and ACID guarantees to deliver a reliable and highly structured data store.
